Fix on the board

Tab next run  ·  ↑↓ move to the string shown  ·  Enter it's fine  ·  ⌘Z undo  ·  Esc close  ·  ? all keys

Fixing notes on the wrong string

A run of notes on the wrong string (an E-string riff shown on the A string, say) takes a couple of moves to fix, wherever the riff comes round.

  1. Pick the notes. Double-click a note to pick its run: the notes around it on that string. Or drag a box around the notes you want; hold ⇧ while clicking or dragging to add to what's picked.
  2. Move them. Press ↓ or ↑ (or the ↓ string / ↑ string buttons). Every picked note goes to the next string at the same pitch: E-string notes are 5 frets lower on the A string, A-string notes 5 frets higher on the E string. A note that can't be played there stays where it is.
  3. Fix it everywhere. If the same notes are on the same strings elsewhere in the song, it offers to fix those too. Show them picks them first, so you can look.
  4. Undo (⌘Z) takes back a whole move in one go.

On the board (press B in the tab view): the keys that work right now are shown under the notes. The basics:

  1. Tab picks the next run that looks off (framed in amber) and brings it on screen.
  2. ↑ or ↓ moves it to the string shown under it; the same notes elsewhere in the song move too. Faint keycaps show where they'd go first.
  3. Enter if it's right as it is: on to the next.
  4. ⌘Z takes a move back. Esc unpicks, then closes.

More keys: ⇧Tab the run before · ⌥Tab every run, not just the ones that look off · ⇧→ ⇧← pick one note more / fewer · one note picked: type its fret, ⌫ deletes it, N adds one after it, ⌥← ⌥→ nudge it a grid step · double-click a string to add a note there · F also fix the same notes (when it asks) · Space loops the picked bars · H without the bass / the song / the bass alone · ← → a bar (or scroll) · − + bars on screen · Home End · ⌘C ⌘V copy bars and paste them from the first bar on screen (for bars the tab left out).

Fixes go into your draft, a copy: on the automatic or an imported tab, the first one makes it, and the tab itself stays as it was. Fixed notes stay where you put them, and the notes around them follow your hand position. One note at a time still works: click it, then ↑ ↓ for the string, a number for the fret.
